hunks.baseline: The instinct that flashed through my mind was not wrong. The old owner of the thin-noodle shop where I had been sitting with Heugung just moments ago had appeared.
hunks.sol: My gut was right. The old owner of the thin-noodle shop where I’d sat with Heugung not long ago had appeared.

hunks.baseline: Something really big had come.
hunks.sol: Something big really had come.

hunks.baseline: I cursed inwardly as I stared at the old shopkeeper.
hunks.sol: I stared at the old shopkeeper, cursing inwardly.

hunks.baseline: No, I was not the only one looking at him. As countless gazes instantly converged on him, a trembling voice emerged from between his age-spotted lips.
hunks.sol: I wasn’t the only one. As countless eyes turned toward him, a trembling voice came from between his age-spotted lips.

hunks.baseline: “U- Utu-ri of the Bai people. I came at the great chieftain’s summons.”
hunks.sol: “U-Utu-ri of the Bai people. I came at the Great Chieftain’s summons.”

hunks.baseline: The Beast Miao King spoke with a grim expression.
hunks.sol: The Beast Miao King spoke, his face grim.

hunks.baseline: “I’ve never seen this face before. Who is he?”
hunks.sol: “I’ve never seen him before. Who is he?”

hunks.baseline: At Baeksang’s signal, the old shopkeeper hurriedly answered.
hunks.sol: At a glance from Baeksang, the old shopkeeper answered at once.

hunks.baseline: “I sell thin noodles near the West Gate of the Outer Palace. I’ve made a living at it for more than half my life.”
hunks.sol: “I sell thin noodles near the West Gate of the Outer Palace. I’ve made my living doing that for more than half my life.”

hunks.baseline: From the old shopkeeper’s words and actions, I learned several new things.
hunks.sol: His words and actions taught me several new things.

hunks.baseline: First. The old shopkeeper’s name was Utu-ri, and he was a member of the Bai people.
hunks.sol: First. The old shopkeeper’s name was Utu-ri, and he was one of the Bai people.

hunks.baseline: Second. Unlike when I had seen him at the noodle shop, Utu-ri spoke clearly and had excellent hearing. In short, he was full of energy. If Jirisan had its baby hero Utu-ri, Nanman had a noodle-selling Utu-ri.[^1]
hunks.sol: Second. Unlike at the noodle shop, Utu-ri could speak clearly and hear perfectly well. In short, he was full of life. Jirisan had its baby hero Utu-ri; Nanman had its noodle-selling Utu-ri.[^1]

hunks.baseline: Third. This Bai elder, whose vitality belied his age, had probably told Baeksang everything he had seen and heard.
hunks.sol: Third. This Bai elder, spry enough to put his age to shame, had probably told Baeksang everything he’d seen and heard.

hunks.baseline: And fourth. I was probably completely screwed.
hunks.sol: And fourth. I was probably fucked.

hunks.baseline: *You fucking bastard, Heugung.*
hunks.sol: *Heugung, you son of a bitch.*

hunks.baseline: What he had said at the noodle shop had been wrong. Very wrong.
hunks.sol: What he’d said at the noodle shop could hardly have been more wrong.

hunks.baseline: *His hearing is bad, my ass.*
hunks.sol: *Bad hearing, my ass.*

hunks.baseline: The thing that had grown dim was my future.
hunks.sol: The only thing looking dim was my future.

hunks.baseline: The shopkeeper, who was supposedly over ninety, had hearing sharp enough to catch every word spoken by the Beast Miao King ten paces away.
hunks.sol: The shopkeeper, supposedly over ninety, had heard the Beast Miao King from ten paces away.

hunks.baseline: “Utu-ri, there is one reason I called you here. I wish to confirm one fact. Do you recognize anyone among those gathered here?”
hunks.sol: “Utu-ri, I called you here to confirm one thing. Do you recognize anyone present?”

hunks.baseline: The old shopkeeper nodded without hesitation at Baeksang’s question, and I realized I had to add one more item to the list of things I had learned.
hunks.sol: The old shopkeeper nodded without hesitation, and I realized I had another item to add.

hunks.baseline: Fifth. Utu-ri possessed not only excellent hearing, but also remarkable eyesight and memory.
hunks.sol: Fifth. Besides excellent hearing, Utu-ri had remarkable eyesight and memory.

hunks.baseline: The reason I could guess that much was simple.
From the moment the old shopkeeper had first set foot in the Western Yao Estate, his gaze had kept darting toward my face.
hunks.sol: That much was easy to tell. From the moment he’d entered the Western Yao Estate, he’d kept stealing glances at my face.

hunks.baseline: “That young man standing over there. The tallest one, with the largest build.”
hunks.sol: “That young man standing over there. The tallest one, with the broad build.”

hunks.baseline: The hand that had trembled like an aspen tree when he set down the bowls of noodles was, for some reason, perfectly still this time.
hunks.sol: When he’d set down our bowls of noodles, his hand had shaken like a leaf. For some reason, the hand pointing at me now was perfectly steady.

hunks.baseline: His finger pointed directly at me. I shut my mouth, the atmosphere around us began to stir, and the script Baeksang had meticulously prepared raced toward its conclusion.
hunks.sol: I shut my mouth. A murmur ran through the crowd, and Baeksang’s carefully prepared script raced toward its conclusion.

hunks.baseline: “Are you certain it was him? There must not be the slightest lie in your answer.”
hunks.sol: “Are you certain it was him? You must not tell even the slightest lie.”

hunks.baseline: The old shopkeeper swallowed hard before answering Baeksang’s question.
hunks.sol: The old shopkeeper swallowed hard before answering.

hunks.baseline: “Yes, without a doubt. I may be old and worn-out, but I’m not so blind that I can’t recognize a customer standing right in front of me. His build was exceptionally large, and he was wearing a tiger mask, so he stood out in my memory.”
hunks.sol: “Yes, without a doubt. I may be old, but I can still recognize a customer who sat right in front of me. He was unusually big, and he wore a tiger mask. That made him particularly memorable.”

hunks.baseline: “Half the people in the Outer Palace must be wearing masks right now. Did you report him as suspicious for no reason beyond that?”
hunks.sol: “Half the people in the Outer Palace must be wearing masks right now. Did you report him as suspicious for that reason alone?”

hunks.baseline: “N-No, that wasn’t it. He lingered nearby, then sat down and ordered noodles. That was when I began to feel something was strange.”
hunks.sol: “N-No, sir. He lingered nearby before sitting down and ordering noodles. That was when I started to find him suspicious.”

hunks.baseline: “Strange? What exactly was strange?”
hunks.sol: “Suspicious? What exactly troubled you?”

hunks.baseline: The old shopkeeper, who had been glancing at me, continued cautiously.
hunks.sol: The old shopkeeper glanced at me, then continued cautiously.

hunks.baseline: “It was because of the mask, sir.”
hunks.sol: “It was the mask, sir.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. Even while eating the noodles, he never took it off. It was as if something terrible would happen if he showed his face.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. He kept it on even while he ate. As though something terrible would happen if anyone saw his face.”

hunks.baseline: “But later, when he drank the broth, the mask must have felt too restrictive, because he raised it slightly. That was the first and only time I saw his face.”
hunks.sol: “But later, when he drank the broth, he seemed to find it too much of a bother and lifted the mask a little. That was the first and only time I saw his face.”

hunks.baseline: So that was when it happened.
hunks.sol: *So that was when.*

hunks.baseline: If I openly revealed my face, they might realize I was Han Chinese. But if I never removed the mask, I would arouse suspicion.

hunks.baseline: So I had deliberately raised it only to just below my nose while eating the noodles, then lifted it properly for a moment at the very end…
hunks.sol: If I showed my whole face, they might realize I was Han Chinese. But keeping the mask on would look suspicious too. I’d deliberately raised it only as far as the bottom of my nose while I ate, then lifted it for a moment at the very end…

hunks.baseline: *Who would have thought that old man, who looked like he could die tomorrow, would notice and remember that?*
hunks.sol: *And the old man who looked ready to die any day saw it and remembered.*

hunks.baseline: At first, my excessive caution had drawn suspicion. Later, overlooking the existence of the old shopkeeper had brought me to this situation.
hunks.sol: First, being too cautious had made him suspicious. Then I’d failed to take the old shopkeeper seriously. Now it had come back to bite me.

hunks.baseline: And now Baeksang was putting an end to it all in his uniquely calm voice.
hunks.sol: Baeksang, in his usual even tone, was bringing the matter to a close.

hunks.baseline: “Were you alone?”
hunks.sol: “Was he alone?”

hunks.baseline: “No. He was sharing a table with some middle-aged man.”
hunks.sol: “No. He shared a table with a middle-aged man.”

hunks.baseline: “Another middle-aged man. What happened after that?”
hunks.sol: “Another middle-aged man. And afterward?”

hunks.baseline: “They left almost at the same time, then headed toward the main road by the West Gate.”
hunks.sol: “They left at almost the same time, then headed toward the main road by the West Gate.”

hunks.baseline: “Do you remember that man’s face?”
hunks.sol: “Do you remember the other man’s face?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes, of course. I’ve lived in the Outer Palace all my life, but he was a stranger I had never seen in the area, so I remember him vividly. The same goes for that young man.”
hunks.sol: “Yes, of course. I’ve lived in the Outer Palace all my life, but I’d never seen him around before, so I remember him clearly. The same goes for that young man.”

hunks.baseline: “Then they were certainly outsiders who entered during the Tribal Grand Council. If we make likenesses of them and investigate, it should be easy to identify them. When did they leave?”
hunks.sol: “Then he must be a tribesman from outside who came for the Tribal Grand Council. A likeness and an inquiry should identify him soon enough. When did they leave?”

hunks.baseline: “It was around Insi, and they stayed for about the time it takes to drink a cup of tea before leaving. The Outer Palace has been setting off firecrackers at regular intervals, so I remember the time clearly.”
hunks.sol: “Around Insi. They stayed about as long as it takes to drink a cup of tea. The Outer Palace has been setting off firecrackers at regular intervals, so I remember the time clearly.”

hunks.baseline: The old shopkeeper answered without a single hesitation. His eyes and voice were filled with certainty.
hunks.sol: The old shopkeeper answered without faltering. His eyes and voice were full of conviction.

hunks.baseline: Having obtained every answer he wanted through the old man, Baeksang gave a small nod.
hunks.sol: Baeksang had gotten every answer he wanted. He gave a small nod.

hunks.baseline: “Thank you for your cooperation. You may withdraw now. I’ll have someone give you a reward separately.”
hunks.sol: “Thank you for your cooperation. You may go. I’ll have someone reward you.”

hunks.baseline: The old shopkeeper bowed repeatedly as he disappeared.
hunks.sol: The old shopkeeper bowed repeatedly as he left.

hunks.baseline: He would probably receive an extremely generous reward for what he had done here. The small stall that had been packed whenever three or four customers showed up would become a large inn, and the wrinkled hands that had boiled noodles would soon be counting silver nyang.
hunks.sol: He’d probably be rewarded handsomely for this. The little stall that filled up with three or four customers would become a large inn, and the wrinkled hands that boiled noodles would count silver nyang instead.

hunks.baseline: But the opportunity he had seized in his old age had returned to me as the worst crisis of my life.
hunks.sol: But the opportunity he’d found in his old age had become the worst crisis of my life.

hunks.baseline: “What a strange matter. Someone who should have been in the Inner Palace secretly slipped out, made contact with an unidentified figure, and then this tragedy occurred immediately afterward.”
hunks.sol: “How strange. A man who ought to have been in the Inner Palace slipped out in secret, met with someone whose identity is unknown, and immediately afterward, this tragedy occurred.”

hunks.baseline: “Your earlier statement has already been exposed as a lie, but even considering what happened at Ailao Mountain, I will give you one final opportunity. Do you wish to make a defense?”
hunks.sol: “Your earlier statement has already been exposed as a lie. Still, in light of what happened at Ailao Mountain, I’ll give you one last chance. Do you have anything to say in your defense?”

hunks.baseline: In the brief moment Baeksang’s low voice pierced my ears, countless thoughts flashed through my mind.
hunks.sol: Countless thoughts flashed through my mind in the brief moment Baeksang’s low voice reached me.

hunks.baseline: By then, the Western Yao Estate had fallen into suffocating silence, and everyone’s gaze was fixed on my face.
hunks.sol: The Western Yao Estate had fallen into suffocating silence. Everyone was looking at me.

hunks.baseline: That was when it happened.
Namho’s finger brushed against my back once again.
hunks.sol: Then Namho’s finger brushed my back again.

hunks.baseline: It was only one word, but I understood exactly what Namho meant.
hunks.sol: One character. It was enough to tell me what he meant.

hunks.baseline: *Get out of here first. We’ll make plans for later.*
hunks.sol: *Get out of here first. Worry about what comes next later.*

hunks.baseline: If Namho had known martial arts, he would have sent me this kind of Sound Transmission. If I had been in his position, I probably would have done the same.
hunks.sol: If Namho had learned martial arts, that was the Sound Transmission he would have sent me. I’d probably have done the same in his place.

hunks.baseline: *Would things have improved if I had simply told them the truth?*
hunks.sol: *Would it have gone better if I’d told the truth?*

hunks.baseline: I answered my own sudden question.
hunks.sol: I answered my own question. No.

hunks.baseline: No.
Of course, things might have been a little better than they were now. But Baeksang had prepared thoroughly. He would have driven me into a situation like this somehow.
hunks.sol: Maybe it would have gone a little better than this. But Baeksang had prepared thoroughly. One way or another, he would have backed me into the same corner.

hunks.baseline: I could insist that the old noodle-shop owner’s statement was a lie, but… please. If Baeksang were stupid enough to fall for that so easily, he never would have made it this far.
hunks.sol: I could claim the old noodle seller was lying, but… come on. If Baeksang were stupid enough to fall for that, he wouldn’t have made it this far.

hunks.baseline: *Besides, a master like Baeksang would realize just by looking at the wounds on the assassins who attacked us that most of them weren’t my handiwork.*
hunks.sol: *And a master like Baeksang could tell from the wounds on the assassins who attacked us that I didn’t kill most of them.*

hunks.baseline: Without Heugung there to corroborate my statement, telling the truth would only make me a shameless culprit.
hunks.sol: Without Heugung here to back me up, telling the truth would only leave me looking like a culprit brazen enough to admit where I’d been.

hunks.baseline: *Though I suppose that would still be better than being a culprit caught lying.*
hunks.sol: *Though I suppose that would beat being a culprit caught in a lie.*

hunks.baseline: Either way, I was trapped. There was no way to avoid it.
hunks.sol: Either way, I was trapped. There was no getting around it.

hunks.baseline: And even now, the situation was racing toward the edge of a cliff.
hunks.sol: And even now, things were hurtling toward the edge.

hunks.baseline: A faint sound pierced my ears through the brief silence.
Blood-soaked grains of sand were crushed beneath leather shoes, while dozens of fluttering hems brushed against the flowers in the garden.
hunks.sol: A faint sound reached me through the brief silence. Leather shoes crushed blood-soaked grains of sand, while dozens of fluttering hems brushed the flowers in the garden.

hunks.baseline: An encirclement had formed around me in an instant.
hunks.sol: In an instant, they had formed a ring around me.

hunks.baseline: At its head stood Baeksang.
hunks.sol: Baeksang stood at its head.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll ask you again. Do you wish to make a defense?”
hunks.sol: “I’ll ask again. Your defense?”

hunks.baseline: A defense.
hunks.sol: My defense.

hunks.baseline: After thinking long and hard, I answered.
hunks.sol: After careful consideration, I answered.

hunks.baseline: “I’m not doing it. This whole thing is too damn filthy, you fucking bastard.”
hunks.sol: “I’m not giving you one. This whole thing’s filthy, you fucking bastard.”

hunks.baseline: They probably had not expected an answer like that. Baeksang looked at me with surprise, then nodded.
hunks.sol: Apparently, that wasn’t the answer they’d expected. Baeksang studied me with a look of surprise, then nodded.

hunks.baseline: “I admit only that I lied. I was stupid.”
hunks.sol: “I admit I lied. That was stupid of me.”

hunks.baseline: “So in the end, you mean to deny it to the very end.”
hunks.sol: “So you intend to deny the rest to the end.”

hunks.baseline: “If you were me, would you admit it? No. I didn’t commit a crime in the first place, so there’s nothing to admit. It just pisses me off that I stepped into an inescapable trap.”
hunks.sol: “Would you admit it in my place? There’s nothing to admit when I haven’t committed a crime. I’m just pissed that I walked into a trap I couldn’t avoid.”

hunks.baseline: “If you believe you have been wronged, surrender quietly. I will determine right and wrong.”
hunks.sol: “If you’ve been wronged, surrender peacefully. I’ll sort out right from wrong.”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah, fucking right, you right-and-wrong bastard.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah, fucking right. Right and wrong, my ass, you prick.”

hunks.baseline: At my scornful reply, Baeksang’s eyes sank into darkness.
hunks.sol: At my scornful answer, Baeksang’s eyes darkened.

hunks.baseline: “Then it cannot be helped.”
hunks.sol: “Then I have no choice.”

hunks.baseline: At the same time—
A dazzling radiance surged from the pure-white blade he drew in a flash. Baeksang lowered his treasured sword, infused with Sword Force, and slowly stepped forward.
hunks.sol: He drew his sword in a flash. Dazzling light surged from its pure-white blade. With the Sword Force-infused weapon lowered at his side, Baeksang took a slow step forward.

hunks.baseline: “The warriors of the Nanman Beast Palace, listen. From this moment onward, we will use our full strength to take the criminal Jin Taekyung into custody. Not a single mistake will be tolerated—”
hunks.sol: “Warriors of the Nanman Beast Palace, listen. We will use our full strength to seize the criminal Jin Taekyung. Not a single mistake will be tolerated—”

hunks.baseline: At that moment, a roar-like shout erupted from somewhere, drowning out the words that were about to leave Baeksang’s mouth.
hunks.sol: A roar cut him off.

hunks.baseline: “Will everyone stop this at once!”
hunks.sol: “All of you, stop!”

hunks.baseline: A powerful wave of aura pressed down from every direction.
hunks.sol: A powerful wave of qi pressed down on us from every direction.

hunks.baseline: The Beast Miao King halted the slowly tightening encirclement with a single command, then glared at Baeksang with blazing eyes.
hunks.sol: The Beast Miao King had halted the tightening ring with a single command. His eyes blazed as he glared at Baeksang.

hunks.baseline: Everyone trembled beneath his fierce aura, but Baeksang did not. He answered in a calm voice.
hunks.sol: Everyone trembled beneath his fierce aura. Baeksang did not.

hunks.baseline: “You can see exactly what I’m doing, Palace Lord. I intend to take the criminal Jin Taekyung into custody here.”
hunks.sol: “Exactly what you see, Palace Lord. I intend to seize the criminal Jin Taekyung here.”

hunks.baseline: “Are you, of all people, the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, shielding the culprit for no reason beyond that?”
hunks.sol: “Are you, the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, shielding a culprit for those reasons alone?”

hunks.baseline: “Ridiculous! That boy is not the culprit. Have you already forgotten what happened at Ailao Mountain? He has neither the justification nor the reason to do something like this!”
hunks.sol: “Nonsense! He is not the culprit. Have you already forgotten what happened at Ailao Mountain? He has no cause or reason to do such a thing!”

hunks.baseline: “But we have a witness who saw him, as well as clear circumstantial evidence.”
hunks.sol: “But we have a witness who saw him, and clear evidence pointing to him.”

hunks.baseline: “But—”
hunks.sol: “That’s—”

hunks.baseline: “Everyone here remembers what happened at Ailao Mountain clearly, myself included. That is why I am taking the trouble to place him under arrest. Of course, if he resists, the order will be to take him dead or alive.”
hunks.sol: “Everyone here remembers what happened at Ailao Mountain, myself included. That is why I’m taking the trouble to capture him. Of course, if he resists, we’ll take him dead or alive.”

hunks.baseline: “We are not finished yet.”
hunks.sol: “I’m not finished.”

hunks.baseline: “If Jin Taekyung leaves this place by force, I will spread a net over heaven and earth across all Nanman and pursue him with everything we have. Before that happens, the other Han Chinese under his command will make excellent examples.”
hunks.sol: “If Jin Taekyung forces his way out of here, I’ll cast a net over heaven and earth across all Nanman and hunt him down with everything we have. Before that, the other Han Chinese under his command will make fine examples.”

hunks.baseline: The Beast Miao King’s eyes widened at the meaning behind Baeksang’s words—he was prepared to risk war with the Central Plains.
hunks.sol: The Beast Miao King’s eyes widened. Baeksang was saying he would risk war with the Central Plains. Yayul Mok shouted, his face contorted.

hunks.baseline: Yayul Mok shouted with a twisted expression.

hunks.baseline: “This is a conversation between tribal chieftains, not between lord and subject. The Young Palace Lord, who has no authority here, should withdraw.”
hunks.sol: “This is a conversation between tribal chieftains, not between lord and subject. The Young Palace Lord has no authority here. Stay out of it.”

hunks.baseline: “But how could you! How could you dare make such a unilateral decision on your own!”
hunks.sol: “But how can you make such a decision on your own?”

hunks.baseline: “A unilateral decision…”
hunks.sol: “On my own…”

hunks.baseline: Baeksang muttered the words softly, then suddenly raised his head and looked at the sky.
hunks.sol: Baeksang murmured the words, then looked up at the sky.

hunks.baseline: The thick darkness that had settled over the surroundings had begun to disperse, and bright light was slowly spreading from the east.
hunks.sol: The thick darkness around us had begun to lift. Light was slowly spreading from the east.

hunks.baseline: “Can you see it? It is already the hour of the Rabbit. Dawn is breaking.”
hunks.sol: “Do you see? It’s already the hour of the Rabbit. Dawn is breaking.”

hunks.baseline: “What does that have to do with this all of a sudden?”
hunks.sol: “What does that have to do with anything?”

hunks.baseline: “What would you say if we began the second day of the Tribal Grand Council right here and now? Of course, the new agenda would be…”
hunks.sol: “What if we begin the second day of the Tribal Grand Council right here? With a new matter on the agenda, of course…”

hunks.baseline: The sword in Baeksang’s hand blazed with even more intense light.
hunks.sol: The sword in Baeksang’s hand shone more fiercely.

hunks.baseline: “Whether Han Chinese Jin Taekyung lives or dies.”
hunks.sol: “Whether the Han Chinese Jin Taekyung lives or dies.”

hunks.baseline: At that moment, a sound like a bell that only one person in this world could hear pierced my ears.
hunks.sol: At that moment, a bell sounded in my ears—a bell only one person in the world could hear.
